claims.text: The as-prepared carbon-supported nanoscale Pt or Pt-alloy catalyst has a nominally metallic surface with low natural coverage of oxidized species.
Potential-cycle pretreatment in alkaline electrolyte increases surface Pt–OH coverage relative to the untreated catalyst.
Pt oxidation and reduction are reversible at 0.5–0.8 V versus RHE under the proposed alkaline conditions.
Increased Pt–OH coverage modifies the local electronic structure of the catalyst.
Increased Pt–OH coverage modifies active-site geometry.
Surface Pt–OH tunes the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Surface Pt–OH lowers the activation energy of key ethanol dehydrogenation steps.
Surface Pt–OH lowers the activation energy of key oxygen-transfer steps.
Surface Pt–OH inhibits the accumulation of poisoning intermediates such as CO-type species.
Suppressing poisoning intermediates maintains an active catalyst surface and improves durability.
Increasing Pt–OH coverage increases ethanol-oxidation current density.
Increasing Pt–OH coverage improves selectivity toward the complete 12-electron oxidation pathway.
Increasing Pt–OH coverage increases selectivity toward CO2 or acetate over partially oxidized products.
Increasing Pt–OH coverage reduces activity degradation during extended operation.
The untreated catalyst is known to exhibit strong but poorly understood ethanol-oxidation activity and selectivity.
The proposed mechanism applies in aqueous alkaline media within the reversible surface-oxidation window.
The proposed mechanism may fail in strongly acidic media.
The proposed mechanism may fail outside the reversible oxidation window because irreversible catalyst changes dominate.

contradictions.description: The mechanism defines the desired selectivity as complete 12-electron oxidation, while the predicted outcome groups acetate with complete oxidation products. Acetate is a partially oxidized ethanol product and is not equivalent to the complete 12-electron pathway to CO2.
